title: Allegations Surrounding Suicide of Sgt Uvaraja s/o Gopal
what_it_is: Allegations Surrounding Suicide of Sgt Uvaraja s/o Gopal

sections.label: Uvaraja's Facebook post claims
sections.summary: Before his passing, he posted on Facebook that superiors and colleagues bullied him, misconduct was covered up, appraisals were unfair, and he was ostracised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Just before his passing, he put up a Facebook post.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: He said that: one, he had been bullied and ill-treated by his superiors and colleagues; two, that some officers’ misconduct had been covered up; three, that his performance appraisals were unfair; and four, that he was ostracised by others at work.

sections.label: Investigations into Uvaraja's allegations
sections.summary: Investigations found some allegations true with prior action taken and officers disciplined, some untrue, and AGC determined no further action needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The investigations found that: one, some of the allegations were true and, in respect of these, there had been investigations at the time the complaints were made, actions had been taken at that time and some officers had been disciplined and punished; and second, some of the allegations made by Uvaraja were untrue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: After the Police had completed their internal investigations, their findings were reviewed by AGC and AGC was satisfied and determined that no further actions were needed.

sections.label: Remarks not aimed at Uvaraja
sections.summary: The remarks were not specifically directed at Uvaraja, but they were not acceptable at all.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The remarks were not specifically directed to, or aimed at, Uvaraja.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But – and this is an important point – their remarks were not acceptable at all.

sections.label: Racial slurs investigated as misconduct
sections.summary: Cases involving racial slurs or casual racism will be investigated as possible misconduct and as a disciplinary breach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Cases involving racial slurs or casual racism will be investigated as possible misconduct and as a disciplinary breach.

sections.label: Ethics seminars against racism
sections.summary: This has been and will be done through platforms like the annual Ethics Seminar and Manpower Department engagement sessions, as racism cannot be tolerated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This has been done and will be done through platforms, such as the annual Ethics Seminar, as well as the Police’s Manpower Department’s engagement sessions with officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We cannot tolerate racism, nor can we tolerate casual racism, snide remarks and jokes which are racist.

sections.label: Superior reprimanded, Uvaraja reassigned
sections.summary: The superior was reprimanded and Uvaraja was temporarily re-assigned to a different unit so both officers could cool off.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The superior was then reprimanded and Uvaraja was temporarily re-assigned to a different unit so that both officers could have some time to cool off.

sections.label: Uvaraja's three complaints investigated
sections.summary: Uvaraja's three complaints were investigated, and for the two made out, action was taken and he was told.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, looking at Uvaraja’s three complaints, in this first part, namely, one, the making of racist remarks; two, the shredding of leave forms; and three, the use of abusive language by his superiors – they were all investigated when he made the complaints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And in respect of the two complaints which were made out, action was taken and Uvaraja was told about the actions that had been taken, and he did not further pursue the complaints.

sections.label: Officers referred for disciplinary action
sections.summary: The officers involved were referred to the Police's Internal Affairs Office and disciplinary action was taken against them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The officers involved were referred to the Police’s Internal Affairs Office for investigations and disciplinary action was taken against them.

sections.label: Uvaraja transferred between work units
sections.summary: At Uvaraja's request, he was transferred to six different work units in nine years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: At Uvaraja’s request, he was transferred to six different work units in nine years.

sections.label: Ongoing criminal and disciplinary investigations
sections.summary: At his death, Uvaraja faced a criminal investigation and an internal disciplinary investigation for disobedience of orders from July 2023 incidents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In summary, at that time when he passed away, he was the subject of three ongoing criminal and disciplinary investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: First, he was under criminal investigation for offences under the Penal Code and the Protection from Harassment Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Second, Uvaraja was under internal disciplinary investigation for disobedience of orders, arising from the incidents in July 2023.

sections.label: April 2023 disciplinary investigation
sections.summary: In April 2023, Uvaraja was under another internal disciplinary investigation for disobedience of orders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Third, in April 2023, he was under another internal disciplinary investigation for disobedience of orders.

sections.label: Uvaraja's leave and medical leave
sections.summary: From 2014 to 2023, Uvaraja took about 120 days' leave yearly, including medical leave and no-pay leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: From 2014 to 2023, Uvaraja took an average of about 120 days’ of leave every year and this, as Members can appreciate, is well beyond normal leave entitlement and much more than what a typical Police officer would get.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Members will see that in 2016, 2017, 2021, 2022 and 2023, he took respectively 70 days, 56 days, 59 days, 80 days and 60 days of medical leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And in addition, in 2015, 2016 and 2022, he took more than 100 days of no-pay leave.

sections.label: Home Team grievance cases
sections.summary: Home Team investigated 310 workplace grievance cases in five years, with 131 substantiated and officers disciplined, including two examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the past five years, the Home Team Departments have investigated 310 cases of allegations of workplace grievances including harassment, discrimination and misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of the 310 cases, 131 were found to be substantiated and the offending officers were subjected to various disciplinary actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2019, two female officers reported that a male officer had touched them inappropriately on multiple occasions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He was sentenced to nine months’ imprisonment and was dismissed from service.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The SI was told by the course coordinator to refrain from making such remarks, but he continued.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He was investigated by the IAO and then charged at the Police Disciplinary Board, where he was found guilty and sentenced to a reduction in rank.

sections.label: Six complaints, three substantiated
sections.summary: Of 29,000 Home Team officers, six complaints were made and three substantiated in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of the 29,000 officers in the Home Team, six complaints, and three were found to be substantiated in the last five years.

sections.label: Home Team and Police numbers
sections.summary: The Home Team has about 29,000 regular and civilian officers plus 7,700 NSFs; the Police has about 10,000 regular officers and 4,000 NSFs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Home Team has about 29,000 regular and civilian officers, with another 7,700 National Service Full-time officers (NSFs).

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police force alone has about 10,000 regular officers and 4,000 NSFs.

sections.label: Sergeant Lim criminal breach of trust
sections.summary: In March 2020, Ground Response Force officer Sergeant Lim was convicted of criminal breach of trust and jailed for misappropriating over $200.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second example, in March 2020, Ground Response Force officer, Sergeant Lim, was convicted in Court for criminal breach of trust and sent to jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He had misappropriated for himself more than $200 in cash from wallets that had been handed over to him while he was on duty for safekeeping.

sections.label: Defending officers against unfair statements
sections.summary: The speaker says officers risk their safety, and unfair statements against officers or the force will be defended robustly.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They go on duty, day in and day out, and put their personal safety on the line, to keep Singapore safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, when we find that statements made against officers or the force are unfair, then we will defend the Police officers and SPF robustly.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think Members will agree that the facts I have set out today paint quite a different picture, compared to the accusations that were made in the posting and the conclusion that some people had come to last year.

sections.label: Standing by and defending officers
sections.summary: The speaker says they will stand by and defend officers who have done no wrong, unlike countries where police are scapegoats.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will stand by our officers and defend them".

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We cannot allow what has happened to the police forces in some other countries to happen in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will set out the facts, defend our officers – clearly and strongly – if they have done no wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And they must know that that is our position, in contrast to the position in many countries where the police and the public service are often made the scapegoats in public debates.

sections.label: Allegations found demonstrably false
sections.summary: Investigations found most allegations demonstrably false, and the AGC decided no further action against involved officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The investigations found that most of the allegations, including that he was ill-treated, bullied, ostracised and unfairly held back in his career, and that other officers’ misconduct had been covered up, were demonstrably false.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) had reviewed the findings and decided that no further action needs to be taken against any of the involved officers.

sections.label: Home Team wrongdoing and harassment cases
sections.summary: In five years, 310 wrongdoing cases were reported across Home Team Departments, including 92 workplace harassment reports, with 50 substantiated and officers dealt with under the Civil Service Disciplinary Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the past five years, 310 cases of wrongdoings were reported across all Home Team Departments, of which 92, or about 30%, were reports of workplace harassment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Our investigations showed that 50 of the 92 cases were substantiated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The officers in all 50 cases were dealt with in accordance with the Civil Service Disciplinary Framework.

sections.label: Allegations found demonstrably false
sections.summary: Investigations found most allegations demonstrably false, and the AGC decided no further action against involved officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The investigations found that most of the allegations, including that he was ill-treated, bullied, ostracised and unfairly held back in his career and that other officers' misconduct had been covered up, were demonstrably false.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) had reviewed the findings and decided that no further action needs to be taken against any of the involved officers.

sections.label: Poor mental health prevalence and strategy
sections.summary: MOH's survey showed poor mental health prevalence rose from 13.4% in 2020 to 17% in 2022, and MOH launched the National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy on 5 October 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Based on Ministry of Health's (MOH) National Population Health Survey 2022, the prevalence of poor mental health had increased from 13.4% in 2020 to 17% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: On 5 October 2023, MOH launched the National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy.

sections.label: Officers not required to report assistance
sections.summary: Officers are not required to report their engagement of such assistance, to assure confidentiality and safety in coming forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To provide officers with the assurance of confidentiality and for them to feel safe to come forward, they are not required to report their engagement of such assistance.

sections.label: Follow-up and investigation scope
sections.summary: A question asks whether Police or psychological teams follow up regularly, and the reply states investigations covered Mr Uvaraja's and others' allegations, including those in that post.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Police or the relevant psychological teams follow up with the officer on a regular basis?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I said in my Statement that the investigations covered not just Mr Uvaraja's allegations but those that have been made by others, and that includes the allegations made in that post.

sections.label: Trust in Singapore Police Force
sections.summary: More than 90% of Singaporeans trust the Singapore Police Force, with trust in excess of 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: People's trust in the Police Force is in excess of 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In Singapore, more than 90% of Singaporeans trust the Singapore Police Force (SPF).

sections.label: Police morale pulse surveys
sections.summary: Pulse surveys suggest Police morale is extremely high, according to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On Police morale, Pulse surveys – surveys which I have described.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There are different kinds of surveys that are done that suggest Police morale is extremely high.

sections.label: Officer falling below standard
sections.summary: An officer who consistently falls below a certain standard for a number of years will be out.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If he falls below a certain standard consistently for a number of years, then he will be out.

sections.label: Committee of Inquiry versus internal investigation
sections.summary: The Member asks why the Minister chose an internal Police investigation instead of a Committee of Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A better way to clear the air may be to appoint a Committee of Inquiry to investigate the case rather than through an internal investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, may I ask the Minister why he has chosen an internal investigation by the Police force itself as opposed to appointing a Committee of Inquiry.

sections.label: Substantiated complaints and Police action
sections.summary: Two complaints were substantiated, investigated when first made, and the Police had taken action against the officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Two of them were found to have been substantiated, but they had been investigated when he had first made the complaint and he did not follow up.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police had actually taken action against the officers.

sections.label: Police assistance and leave given
sections.summary: The Police provided psychological assistance, days off and leave, including 150 days in 2015 and 286 days the next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What the Police force can say is that they did everything they can to help him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They provided psychological assistance; they gave him days off and they gave him leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you take 2015, if a person does not turn up for work for 150 days –100 days of no-pay leave and 40 days of medical leave – I think it is an extraordinary organisation that gives that level of flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And then, the next year, no-pay leave of 216 days and 70 days of medical leave – that makes it 286 days out of 360.

sections.label: Investigation and AGC review
sections.summary: The matter was investigated thoroughly, the AGC reviewed the findings, and the speaker then reviewed them personally.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Which is why it was investigated thoroughly, and I had the AGC review those findings, and then I reviewed them myself.
